metadata.note: Sylvania Railroad / Sylvania Central Railway, Rocky Ford (junction with the Central of Georgia Savannah - Macon main line, now NS Savannah District) northeast to Sylvania, Screven County GA, 14.7 mi, via Parker, Thomasboro, Woodcliff, Zeigler and Waters. One physical line drawn as four features with identical geometry, split under Rule 4 at each change of operator: Sylvania Railroad 1885-1902 (foreclosure 5 Aug 1902); Sylvania Central 1903-1905, 1916-1934 and 1944-1949 [OPEN]; Sylvania and Girard (lessee) 1906-1915; Sylvania Railway (lessee) 1935-1943. Central of Georgia stock control from 1902/03 is not a split - the Sylvania companies remained the named operators. Not drawn (Rule 1): the freight-only tail after the last confirmed passenger year (1949, [OPEN]) to abandonment by the Central of Georgia on 27 Mar 1954. Not folded in: the separate Brinson Railway / Savannah & Northwestern / Savannah and Atlanta line through Sylvania (its own report, savannah_and_atlanta_railway.txt). No horsecar era (steam from opening). The research report recommended splitting only at 1902/03 and deferring the two lessee splits until the lessees' identities are sourced; the lessee features were drawn on the caller's instruction, with that caveat in their notes. Colours #8F30BF, #4BA661, #56B6BF and #BF7056 are new to the dataset.

Simplified Douglas-Peucker 8 m, trim_reversals; no spurs.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] passenger end: the Sylvania Central 1944-1949 segment ends at 1949, the last CONFIRMED year (Dec 1949 mixed-train schedule in the Feb 1952 Official Guide); service may have run to 1951-52 and ended no later than the 27 Mar 1954 abandonment. Next: Screven County / Sylvania Telephone papers 1950-54 (Georgia Historic Newspapers) and the ICC Finance Docket for the 1953/54 abandonment. (2) Lessee identities: who the Sylvania and Girard Railroad (1906-1915) and the Sylvania Railway Co. (1935-1943/44) were, and whether passengers ever saw their names - the Feb 1906 Guide printed the schedule under the Sylvania Central name one month into the S&G lease; SOURCE CONFLICT on the Sylvania Railway lease end, railga.com 1944 vs SNAC 1954. (3) 1917-1948 interior: no direct passenger evidence between the 1916 Equipment Register (2 coaches) and the Dec 1949 schedule; drawn continuous by inference. (4) Aug 1902 - May 1903 operator: trains ran (Mar 1903 complaint) but whether the receiver, the purchaser or the Central of Georgia ran them is not established; the Sylvania Railroad feature ends 1902 and the Sylvania Central starts 1903. (5) The first dated Sylvania Central timetable is Feb 1906; 1903-1905 rest on the incorporation date and the Mar 1903 complaint. (6) 1886-1900 rest on the 1885 timetable and the 1894 equipment listing. (7) Original 1885 gauge not established (standard by 1915/16); 1885-1909 Sylvania terminal site not checked against a period map.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Built 2026-11-09 to Rule 1: the post-passenger freight operation (after 1949 [OPEN]) to the 27 Mar 1954 abandonment is not drawn.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Built 2026-11-09 to Rule 5: steam from opening (1 May 1885); nothing to trim.

segments.note: Sylvania Railroad (chartered 3 Jan 1884; P. H. Daffin of Savannah, president), Sylvania - Waters - Zeigler - Woodcliff - Thomasboro - Parker - Rocky Ford, steam from opening. Passenger trains began Friday 1 May 1885 (company notice dated Sylvania, May 1 1885, Savannah Morning News 5 May 1885 p.5: leave Sylvania 10:30 am, arrive Rocky Ford 12 m; leave Rocky Ford 1:15 pm, arrive Sylvania 2:10 pm, connecting with the Central Railroad's day passenger trains; same paper 2 May 1885: 'the running of a regular schedule begun yesterday'). 1894 Official Railway List (via railga.com): 15 miles, 1 locomotive, 1 passenger car. Receivership c. Aug 1901 (receiver W. M. Hobby); sold at foreclosure at Sylvania 5 Aug 1902 to H. W. Johnson for Mills B. Lane, acting for the Central of Georgia (Savannah Morning News 6 Aug 1902 p.6). The segment ends at 1902 because that sale ended the Sylvania Railroad's operation; trains kept running (a March 1903 Railroad Commission complaint about track 'dangerous to the traveling public', Savannah Morning News 8 Mar 1903 p.1), but who ran them between Aug 1902 and the Sylvania Central's incorporation on 2 May 1903 is not established. Years 1886-1900 are not individually evidenced beyond the 1894 equipment listing; drawn continuous because nothing suggests an interruption. Headway 1440 min is the one 1885 round trip a day - an estimate, not a measured interval, and not known for later years.
sources: Segment-level: start from the dated 1 May 1885 company timetable (Savannah Morning News 5 May 1885, 2 May 1885, 22 Jun 1885); end from the 5 Aug 1902 foreclosure sale (Savannah Morning News 6 Aug 1902) and the Mar 1903 complaint; 1894 equipment from railga.com - as read in research/branches/sylvania_central_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-09); the tracer did not re-open these pages. Interior years 1886-1900 inferred.

segments.note: Sylvania Central Railway (incorporated 2 May 1903 per the ICC valuation; controlled by the Central of Georgia through stock ownership, which is not a Rule 4 split - the Sylvania Central remained the named operator). Superintendent W. M. Hobby, Sylvania. Start 1903 is the incorporation year; the line was carrying the 'traveling public' in March 1903, but the first dated Sylvania Central passenger timetable found is the Feb 1906 Official Guide, so 1903-1905 service is inferred, not timetabled. Ends 1905 because the road was leased to the Sylvania and Girard Railroad from 1 Jan 1906 (separate feature). Headway 720 min is ESTIMATED from the Feb 1906 Guide's two round trips (one month into the lease), not a figure for 1903-1905.
sources: Segment-level: start from the 2 May 1903 incorporation (ICC valuation, via the WikiProject Trains ICC valuations page) and the Mar 1903 complaint (Savannah Morning News 8 Mar 1903); end from the 1 Jan 1906 S&G lease (railga.com sylgir/sylcen); headway from the Feb 1906 Guide image on railga.com - as read in research/branches/sylvania_central_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-09); the tracer did not re-open these pages. No timetable inside 1903-1905 was found.

segments.note: Sylvania Central again operating after the Sylvania and Girard lease ended (S&G dissolved 1 Dec 1915 per railga.com; the ICC valuation dates the lease end six months after its 30 Jun 1915 valuation date). Oct/Nov 1916 Official Railway Equipment Register: 15 miles, standard gauge, 2 locomotives, 2 coaches. Ends 1934 because the road was leased to the Sylvania Railway Co. from 1935 (separate feature). No direct passenger evidence (timetable, Guide entry or news item) was found for 1917-1934: the interior is drawn continuous by inference from the 1916 coaches and the 1949 schedule, with no source mentioning a suspension. Headway 720 min carries the 1906 two-round-trip pattern forward and is an ESTIMATE with no timetable behind it for these years.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the start and end years are lease boundaries (railga.com sylgir, sylvry; ICC valuation) and the 1916 Equipment Register image on railga.com shows 2 coaches, but no source checked establishes passenger service or its frequency in 1917-1934 - as read in research/branches/sylvania_central_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-09); the tracer did not re-open these pages.

segments.note: Sylvania Central again operating after the Sylvania Railway lease (railga.com: lease 1935-1944; SNAC says it ran to abandonment in 1954 - see the Sylvania Railway feature's source_conflict). The Feb 1952 Official Guide (schedules eff. 30 Sep 1951), in the Central of Georgia section under 'SYLVANIA CENTRAL RAILWAY COMPANY' (D. C. Rogers president, CofG officers; S. J. Newton supt. and agent, Sylvania): 'Mixed passenger and freight trains leave Rocky Ford daily, except Saturday and Sunday, 10:10 a.m., arrive Sylvania (14.7 miles) 11:15 a.m. and returns, leaving Sylvania 8:00 a.m., arrive Rocky Ford 8:45 a.m. ... December, 1949.' The Guide's station index lists Parker, Waters, Zeigler and Sylvania against the Sylvania Central with no freight-only dagger. [OPEN] END: passenger (mixed-train) service is confirmed to 1949 by that December 1949 schedule. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when the mixed train actually stopped; it may have run into 1951-52 (still printed, undaggered, in the Feb 1952 Guide) and ended no later than the abandonment of 27 Mar 1954. Do not extend without evidence; in particular do not extend to 1954 - the freight-only tail under CofG control to abandonment is excluded under Rule 1, and the 1954 'last train out of Woodcliff' photo is not passenger evidence. 1944-1948 are not individually evidenced (railga.com has 1947 photos of engine 103 and the Woodcliff depot, not of a passenger train). Headway 1440 min is the one weekday mixed round trip of Dec 1949, not a measured interval.
sources: Segment-level: end from the Dec 1949 schedule in the Feb 1952 Official Guide (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt); start from the 1944 end of the Sylvania Railway lease on railga.com - as read in research/branches/sylvania_central_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-09); the tracer did not re-open these pages. End year is [OPEN]; 1944-1948 inferred.

segments.note: Sylvania and Girard Railroad Co., lessee of the Sylvania Central 1 Jan 1906 - 1 Dec 1915 (ICC valuation: ten-year lease, rent $3,600/yr cut to $1,800 from 1 Jul 1912; railga.com: S&G dissolved 1 Dec 1915). Split out under Rule 4 because a lease counts. CAVEAT: the Feb 1906 Official Guide, one month into the lease, still printed the passenger schedule under 'SYLVANIA CENTRAL RAILWAY' with the same superintendent (W. M. Hobby): leave Sylvania 7:00 a.m. daily and 2:00 p.m. daily except Sunday, arrive Rocky Ford (15 miles) 8:15 a.m. and 3:15 p.m.; return 9:20 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., arrive Sylvania 10:30 a.m. and 5:30 p.m.; connection with the Central of Georgia. So passengers may have seen the Sylvania Central name throughout; no S&G-named timetable was found, and who the S&G was (CofG affiliate or local promoters; the name suggests a projected extension toward Girard, Burke County, which no source says was built) is not established. 1907-1915 are not individually timetabled. Headway 720 min is ESTIMATED from the Feb 1906 two round trips.
sources: Segment-level: lease dates from the ICC valuation (WikiProject Trains ICC valuations page) and railga.com sylgir; Feb 1906 Guide image on railga.com - as read in research/branches/sylvania_central_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-09); the tracer did not re-open these pages. 1907-1915 service and the lessee's identity not established.

Headway 1440 min is an ESTIMATE (the 1949 one-round-trip pattern), not a figure for these years.
